stances.claim: 'Lovely longevity' is the senior-citizen aspiration to put 'more life to our years under God's providence, not just adding more years to our lives' -- pursued through chat groups including 'Happy Seniors 100,' 'Sousai 100,' 'Retired SC Justices 100+,' and 'Team Lenggries 100 and Beyond.'

The fountain-of-youth search is ancient -- Ponce de Leon 1513 Florida (lifespan then 32); Egyptian pharaohs and Chinese emperors; Lao-tzu's descendant Tao promising immortality to men 'who could sexually satisfy their partners a dozen times per day'; Old Testament Abraham (100) and Sarah (90) with Isaac; Islamic tradition that Abraham's firstborn with Hagar was Ishmael.
Science and medicine 'have unquestionably prolonged life' -- Fleming's 1928 penicillin; anesthesia; vaccines; sanitation; biotechnology + AI promise for cancer, heart disease, dementia.

Dan Buettner's 'Blue Zones' (Netflix four episodes) covered five places with 10x more centenarians than the rest of the US per capita: Okinawa, Ikaria, Loma Linda CA, Sardinia, Nicoya. Eight commonalities: plant-based diet; natural body movement; social life; sense of purpose ('ikigai' = 'a reason for being'); adequate sleep; reduced stress; stopping at 80% full; growing own fruits/vegetables.

Singapore is the surprise -- lifespan 84 (vs global 73) due to 'policy nudges to eat healthier, an efficient public transport system and park network to encourage people to walk more, imposing an expensive vehicle entry fee to the city center that lessened pollution, and a world-class health care and competitive education systems' -- but 'very expensive,' first-world per capita above the Americans.

one_paragraph_summary: CJ surveys the senior-citizen quest for 'lovely longevity' -- 'the art of putting more life to our years under God's providence, not just adding more years to our lives' -- pursued through chat groups including 'Happy Seniors 100,' 'Sousai 100,' 'Retired SC Justices 100+,' and 'Team Lenggries 100 and Beyond.' The fountain-of-youth search is not new: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de Leon roamed Florida's 'marshes and jungles' in 1513 when average lifespan was 32; Egyptian pharaohs and Chinese emperors directed their minions to find 'magical ways to everlasting life'; Lao-tzu's descendant Tao 'promised immortality to men who could sexually satisfy their partners a dozen times per day'; the Old Testament records Abraham (100) and Sarah (90) with Isaac, while Islamic tradition records that Abraham's firstborn with Hagar (Sarah's handmaiden) was Ishmael. Science and medicine have unquestionably prolonged life: Fleming's 1928 penicillin healed bacterial ailments; anesthesia relieved surgical pain; vaccines and sanitation conquered epidemics; viruses 'can one day be subdued'; biotechnology with AI 'will discover cures for cancer, heart diseases, dementia, and other existing incurables.' Beyond science is Dan Buettner's bestseller 'Blue Zones' (Netflix four-part series), which visited five places with 10x more centenarians per capita than the rest of the US: Okinawa, Ikaria, Loma Linda CA, Sardinia, and Nicoya. Eight commonalities: (1) plant-based diet, mostly fruits and veggies with very little meat; (2) natural body movement -- all-day walking, gardening, chores; (3) social life with relatives, singing/dancing with friends, community mingling; (4) sense of purpose -- 'ikigai' ('a reason for being'); (5) adequate sleep in quality and quantity; (6) reduced stress; (7) stopping eating at 80% full; (8) growing own fruits/vegetables or easy access. The surprise inclusion is Singapore -- lifespan risen to 84 (vs global 73) due to 'policy nudges to eat healthier, an efficient public transport system and park network to encourage people to walk more, imposing an expensive vehicle entry fee to the city center that lessened pollution, and a world-class health care and competitive education systems' -- though very expensive (first-world per-capita income higher than the Americans). CJ is currently in Germany with Team Lenggries 100 in the foothills of the Bavarian Alps (a 'ritzy suburb' ~50km south of Munich) and in nearby Swiss towns around Lake Geneva, where in 1931 Dr. Paul Niehans founded 'living cell therapy,' continued by his 'capable acolyte' Dr. Siegfried Block and later by daughter Dr. Petra Block and grandson Dr. Daniel Block. Germany today has 500+ cell-therapy specialists and ~5,000 occasional prescribers. Almost a century of practice (1931-present) brought 'youthful looks and revitalized health' to Pope Pius XII (who appointed Niehans to the Papal Academy of Sciences in 1955, 'making him a worthy successor to penicillin discoverer Fleming'), Charles de Gaulle, Emperor Hirohito, King Abdullah of Saudi Arabia, Harry Truman, Marilyn Monroe, Madonna, and Pablo Picasso. The mechanism: cells and minute cell-unions from unborn or young 'cancer-resistant mountain sheep' from Dr. Siegfried Block GmbH's herd of ~700 are extracted under clinical conditions in its EU-certified laboratory, suspended in natural solution, and injected within 40 minutes of sheep-slaying into the patient's buttocks (8-10 shots); 'newly injected live cells will stimulate, revitalize, and restore the patient's weakened tissues and organs.' Will it work for Team Lenggries 100? Will it 'make old age worth living'? 'I will tell you within four to 12 weeks when the treatment is supposed to fully work its wonders.'
